title: Uneven rate smoothing causing sticky throttles across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments experienced sustained 429s during a regional capacity flapping event. Symptoms included opaque throttles, long-lived degraded throughput for specific tenants, and failed automatic fallback to permissive model variants. Impact window: ~2026-03-08 15:12 UTC to 2026-03-09 03:40 UTC for the majority of affected tenants.

Root cause hypothesis (validated): An interaction between the EWMA-based rate smoothing in the proxy admission controller and the tenant credit reconciliation logic in the orchestrator produced a negative credit bias that did not recover after capacity stabilized. The smoothing algorithm uses local wall-clock alignment to compute the decay window; when hybrid routing triggered cross-region failover or a Dedicated->Hosted fallback, the orchestrator and the proxy observed different epoch boundaries (clock skew + batching alignment). The result was a sticky dampening factor applied to tenant credit (effectively double-decaying credits) that prevented normal replenishment for multiple hours. In Private deployments, a stale TTL on the local cache exacerbated the effect because reconciliation was delayed.

Why this was missed: Unit tests covered single-node smoothing and credit refill, integration tests used synchronized clocks; no end-to-end test covered multi-region failover with partial clock drift and hybrid routing. Telemetry surfaced increased reject ratios but did not map them to epoch alignment mismatch.

Immediate mitigations applied: 1) Emergency override released at 2026-03-08 16:20 UTC to bypass EWMA smoothing for affected tenant groups (customers flagged by SRE) which restored baseline throughput within minutes. 2) Orchestrator forced a full credit reconciliation and epoch resync for all impacted tenants at 2026-03-08 17:05 UTC. 3) Short-term config change: reduce smoothing decay factor and shorten window for 12 hours to allow credits to recover while we investigate.

Permanent fix plan: 1) Align epoch calculation: move to a coordinator-driven epoch token signed by the orchestrator and validated by proxies to remove reliance on local wall-clock alignment. 2) Make credit reconciliation idempotent and additive rather than subtractive when epoch mismatch detected. 3) Add explicit failover path tests that simulate clock skew and hybrid routing. 4) Instrument additional metrics: epoch_mismatch_count, credit_underflow_events, reconciliation_duration, per-tenant-smoothing-multiplier. 5) Backfill a one-time pass to repair customers still impacted by negative-credit residuals.

Customer comms: SRE sent targeted updates to impacted customers (list in attachments) and posted a status page entry linking to the ongoing incident report. Post-incident follow-up will include a technical write-up and API guidance to customers with on-prem agents.
updates: 2026-03-08 16:20 UTC - Emergency override applied to bypass EWMA smoothing for flagged tenants (deployed by SRE).
2026-03-08 17:05 UTC - Orchestrator full credit reconciliation and epoch resync executed (manual run + automation added).
2026-03-08 21:30 UTC - Rollout of temporary smoothing window reduction completed across Hosted fleet. Monitoring shows reject ratio returning to acceptable thresholds for most tenants.
2026-03-09 02:10 UTC - Private deploy customers asked to run provided reconciliation script; 3 of 4 reported restored throughput.
2026-03-10 09:15 UTC - Root cause analysis draft completed; technical owners assigned for permanent fixes.
2026-03-14 11:00 UTC - Spike PR created to introduce coordinator-signed epoch tokens and unit tests (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rate-control/pull/2176).
resolution_summary: Emergency bypass + forced reconciliation restored service. Permanent fix will centralize epoch tokens and harden reconciliation logic. Expect rollout over two sprints followed by canary and wide rollout.
next_steps: Implement coordinator-signed epoch tokens (owner: infra-team, estimate: 5 points).
Change reconciliation to additive idempotent model and add unit/integration tests (owner: quota-team, estimate: 3 points).
Add end-to-end failover test harness that simulates clock skew and hybrid routing (owner: qa, estimate: 5 points).
Schedule customer backfill run and confirm via monitoring (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-20).
